solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Possibly "bogs", reader!

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters that follow are only one of several arrangements they could take

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as the fodder

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside to the reader suggesting some euphemism might mean toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: GARDEROBES is a word that, like cloakroom, came to be used for privies in medieval castles.
explanation.definitionFit: A garderobe was a medieval privy, so garderobes could indeed be called bogs, British slang for toilets.

clue.text: People of mixed heritage in an English county to the west

indicators.note: in a down clue, being to the west means coming first, so the article is placed ahead of the county

parts.note: taken as written
Glos is the abbreviation for Gloucestershire, a county in western England

explanation.surface: A description of a mixed community living in some county in the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo is used, especially in North America, for a person of English descent among people of other backgrounds.

clue.text: It sounds like father will totter

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to rely on how the words are spoken, not on their spelling

parts.note: dad'll is the spoken contraction of dad will

explanation.surface: A worried prediction that an elderly father is going to wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddle is a dialect verb meaning to walk unsteadily, as a toddler or an old person does.

clue.text: Bore keen to be heard

indicators.note: something to be heard is judged by ear, so we want a word that is pronounced like the next one

parts.note: eager is a synonym of keen

explanation.surface: A tedious person who is keen to have their voice heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a dull person, but it is the tidal wave that runs up some rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eger, also spelt eagre, is a tidal bore, a wave surging up an estuary such as the Severn.

clue.text: Cleric joined by important lady and little girl for a game

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a clergyman
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
sis is a short form of sister

explanation.surface: A vicar, a grand lady and a small girl join together to play something.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversis is an old card game in which the aim is to take as few tricks as possible.

clue.text: Packaging article in glittery stuff

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the second word's letters

parts.note: bling is showy jewellery
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item wrapped in sparkly gift wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Baling is pressing goods such as hay or cloth into bundles, a form of packing them up.

clue.text: Each road comes to Bury (up north!)

parts.note: ea is the abbreviation for each
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Every road leads to Bury, the town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town, but it is the verb; 'up north' says the word is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Eard is a Scots verb meaning to inter, put into the earth.

clue.text: Man changing direction finally — the spoke is put in here

definitions.text: the spoke is put in here

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is a compass point, and it is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man turning round at the end of a bike or wheel repair.
explanation.walkthrough: The W (west) at the end of FELLOW turns to E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: A felloe is the outer rim of a wheel, into which the ends of the spokes are fitted.

clue.text: Attacks in East Anglian region on fateful day

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece being on another means it sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the Norfolk Broads, a network of lakes and rivers in East Anglia
the Ides of March, the day Julius Caesar was murdered

explanation.surface: Raids on the Norfolk countryside on an ill-omened date.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal or written attack, originally the firing of all guns on one side of a ship.

clue.text: Politically committed nurse reaching maturity

parts.note: EN, enrolled nurse
no word here plainly gives this letter; the blogger reads it as G for general
to come of age is to reach maturity

explanation.surface: A nurse growing up into someone with political convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The G is not clearly clued in the printed text; the Times for the Times blogger took it as G for general, so a word may have been lost from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Engagé is a French borrowing describing a writer or artist actively committed to a political cause.

clue.text: Feast cut short after setback around a camp

indicators.note: a setback here is read as being set back to front, so the letters are turned round
around means the following letter is wrapped inside
something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: regale can be a noun meaning a feast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A banquet curtailed after some reverse at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: REGALE loses its last letter, is turned round, and then takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is a defensive camp, originally of wagons drawn into a circle in South Africa.

clue.text: One-time agricultural king not totally in charge

indicators.note: not the whole thing means the final letter is left off

parts.note: George, the name of several English kings
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A former farming monarch who only partly runs things.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgic, after Virgil's poem on farming, is an old adjective meaning relating to agriculture or rural life.

clue.text: They arranged property deals, settling scores with passion involved

indicators.note: settling here means rearranging into a new order, as when scores are sorted out

parts.note: taken as written
heat is intense passion

explanation.surface: Estate agents who settled old grudges in a fit of emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheators were officials who dealt with escheats, the reversion of property to the Crown when there was no heir.

clue.text: Something in the pipeline from divine being confronting wickedness

indicators.note: to confront is to stand face to face, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a deity
a synonym

explanation.surface: A battle between a deity and sin that is still being planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pipeline' sounds like something being planned; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-devil is a scraper sent through an oil or gas pipeline to clean it.

clue.text: Vehicle in snow taken the wrong way — motorway to be avoided

indicators.note: what is avoided is left out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: misled means led in the wrong direction
the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A sleigh driven off course in the snow, keeping off the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wrong way' suggests a reversal, but it is part of a phrase meaning misled. The M1 runs from London to Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled is a sledge, a vehicle with runners for travelling over snow.

clue.text: Phantoms perform in a story from the east

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters
in an across clue, coming from the east means read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a lie is a story, a fib
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Ghosts acting in an oriental tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Eidola, plural of eidolon, are spectres or phantom images.

clue.text: Beer is carried by my ship or train

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Beer transported by my vessel or railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaler is a vessel or railway train used for carrying coal.

clue.text: Biological substance — a collection of books has current information

parts.note: taken as written
NT, the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
I is the symbol for electric current
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A library said to hold up-to-date facts.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a substance that provokes the body to produce antibodies.

clue.text: One issuing instruction at random? At random!

indicators.note: the repeated phrase now tells us to mix up the letters in no fixed order

parts.note: the first occurrence taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone giving orders haphazardly, with a mocking echo.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark joins the definition to the fodder; the second 'At random!' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandator is the person who gives a mandate, an authoritative order or commission.

clue.text: Nail in Jock's table?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for a spike or nail, the source of brad
second meaning: Scots for a board or table

explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, so 'Jock's' marks a Scots word. Two unrelated obscure words share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Brod is both an old word for a nail or goad and a Scots form of board, meaning table.

clue.text: One wise person's full of energy providing learned introductions

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, with the possessive s
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A wise person bursting with energy who gives scholarly prefaces.
explanation.definitionFit: An isagoge is a scholarly introduction to a subject, from the Greek for leading in.

clue.text: Attractive part of hospital with decoration

parts.note: ENT, the ear, nose and throat department
icing decorates a cake

explanation.surface: A hospital ward made appealing by some ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticing means tempting or alluring, so it is a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Africans — any number with weapons around island

parts.note: n stands for any number in maths

indicators.note: around means the weapons enclose the following letter

parts.note: guns are weapons
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Armed Africans surrounding an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nguni are a group of southern African peoples including the Zulu and Xhosa.

clue.text: Pull up vehicle and embrace

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to pet is to fondle or embrace

explanation.surface: Stopping the car for a cuddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' suggests stopping a car, but here it means to reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to call them in for a reprimand, the same idiom as pulling them up.

clue.text: Local fellow admits blunder that's set up old-style plague

indicators.note: admitting something lets it inside

parts.note: mun is a dialect form of man

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A villager whose mistake brings back an old pestilence.
explanation.definitionFit: Murren is an archaic spelling of murrain, a plague or infectious disease of cattle.

clue.text: Soldiers heading for home on Irish monument

parts.note: soldiers are men

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of home
Ir is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Troops going home past an Irish memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A menhir is a single tall standing stone, a prehistoric monument.

clue.text: Not in favour of using some imagination

indicators.note: some of a word means only a part of its letters, a run within it

parts.note: letters two to five

explanation.surface: Opposing something by drawing on creative thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Absolutely drunk, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by the sound means the answer is pronounced like the word clued

parts.note: juiced is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone completely intoxicated, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: In many British accents the opening of the answer is said like 'joo', so it matches juiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuced is an old-fashioned intensifier meaning extremely or confoundedly, as in deuced awkward.

clue.text: Boat artist incorporating hearts in monogram

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into its body

parts.note: a tug is a boat
RA, Royal Academician
H for hearts, as in card notation

explanation.surface: A boat painter working a heart into someone's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A tughra is the elaborate calligraphic monogram of an Ottoman sultan.

clue.text: Prophet without hint of any foot protection

indicators.note: without means that letter is removed

parts.note: Hosea, an Old Testament prophet

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of any, the one dropped

explanation.surface: A prophet going barefoot, without a scrap of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose means stockings or socks, which cover and protect the feet.

clue.text: African prince turning up in shortened garment usually worn by women

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: Ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince or ruler

indicators.note: shortened means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An African prince appearing in a cut-down women's garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the long draped garment worn chiefly by women of South Asia.

clue.text: Report of horse in gutter

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer is said like the word clued

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white

explanation.surface: News of a horse lying in a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rone is a Scots word for a roof gutter or drainpipe.

clue.text: Travelling box one sailor brought into settlement

indicators.note: something brought into another is placed inside it

parts.note: pah, or pa, is a Maori fortified village
Roman numeral one
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sea chest carried by a seaman into a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitarah is a box or basket used in India for carrying clothes on a journey.

clue.text: Cleansed from terrible sin — looking embarrassed about it

indicators.note: being about something means going around it

parts.note: someone looking embarrassed is red in the face

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone washed clean of awful wrongdoing and blushing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash with clean water, so rinsed is a synonym of cleansed.

clue.text: King at home has duck first as appetiser

indicators.note: first places this piece at the front, ahead of the rest

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket
Rex, Latin for king
in means at home

explanation.surface: A monarch dining at home starts with duck as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appetiser' looks like a starter course; it is a hormone that stimulates appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Orexin is a brain hormone that stimulates appetite, so it is literally an appetite-raiser.

clue.text: Like some surgeons, precise when handling damaged retina

indicators.note: handling something means holding it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: very means precise, as in the very thing

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye surgeon working carefully on a damaged retina.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to eye surgery, but the surgeons are animal doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterinary describes the medicine of animals, so vets are veterinary surgeons.
